claims.text: Blast radius: everything an attacker can reach with what one compromised part holds; least privilege is how you keep it small.
A PostgreSQL superuser bypasses all permission checks except the right to log in. In PostgreSQL a user is a role with the LOGIN attribute (CREATE USER is CREATE ROLE with LOGIN).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, Role Attributes (superuser status, login privilege); CREATE USER

claims.text: RabbitMQ permissions: configure = create/delete exchanges and queues, write = publish to an exchange, read = consume from a queue; each is set per user per vhost, and a vhost groups exchanges and queues.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ 4.1 docs, Access Control (How Permissions Work); Virtual Hosts

The official postgres image creates the user named by POSTGRES_USER with superuser power at initialization.

claims.text: The captured output masks the payments row count because other scripts in the repository create refunds, so the count changes between runs.

threat-model.md records the shared PostgreSQL user as P1 and the shared RabbitMQ user as P2, both deferred to release 3 of multi-shop-data-rollout.md, which already moves services to a role without BYPASSRLS.
On staging the NetworkPolicy db allows notifications (among others) to reach the db Pod on port 5432, the one server that holds the services' databases (stated in sections 4 and 8).
PostgreSQL superusers (and roles with BYPASSRLS) always bypass row-level security policies.

Per-service roles and broker users shrink the blast radius to roughly what each service needs; a separate server per service pays off only when isolation beyond permissions on a shared server is needed.

A new reporting job should get its own read-only user rather than donhang; splitting RabbitMQ users can go before release 3 if forged messages worry the team more, since it does not depend on row-level security.
After release 3, the script should show Notifications' own role, superuser no, and permission errors for payments and user_entity if that role has no rights there.
claims.source_hint: threat-model.md @ stage-4 line 68 (role per service, rights only on its own database); PostgreSQL docs, Privileges
